latch.dataset: 12 SWE-bench Lite instances (1 repository, sympy) plus 9 upstream bug fixes

slopgate_comparison.caveat: These two benchmarks measure different tasks, so the columns are parallel in shape, not in meaning. Slopgate removes injected slop and proves the rewrite keeps behavior; Latch proves that a PR's fix is correct. Slopgate's numbers are quoted from its own repo (link above), not re-run by Latch. The datasets, the instances and the judges differ, and Latch's instance set is smaller and pools hand-built wrong patches with real fixes.

comparison: On real fixes Latch proved 7/21 (33.3%) against Otter's 31.4% (TDD-Bench-Verified) and AssertFlip's 43.6% (SWT-Bench-Verified) fail-to-pass rates, but with only 21 cases, on different benchmarks and a different pass condition (proof test plus repo suite plus revert check), so treat it as a small-sample indication, not a like-for-like comparison.
caveat: Small sample: the cases here are few, single runs, with an LLM that is not deterministic, so the rates carry wide uncertainty. The wrong patches are constructed by hand (not agent output). The baselines use different benchmarks and a different, weaker success condition (fail-to-pass only, no revert check, no wrong-patch test), so the numbers are not directly comparable.
